title: The Immune Response to Viruses
text: When a virus infects the body, the immune system mounts a coordinated response. Innate immunity provides the first line of defense, with macrophages and natural killer cells attacking infected cells. Infected cells release interferons, signaling proteins that warn neighboring cells and activate immune defenses. Dendritic cells present viral antigens to T cells, activating the adaptive immune response. Cytotoxic T cells (CD8+) directly kill virus-infected cells, while helper T cells (CD4+) coordinate the immune response. B cells produce virus-specific antibodies that neutralize the virus or mark it for destruction. Memory T and B cells formed during the infection provide long-term immunity against future encounters with the same virus.
